blogs.title: The Simple Twist That Tames Diffusion Models: Orthogonal Finetuning Explained
blogs.description: A plain-language tour of Orthogonal Finetuning (OFT), a method that gently ‘rotates’ a model’s neurons so it learns new skills without forgetting how to make great images. Learn why preserving neuron relationships keeps semantic quality intact and how OFT adds zero inference overhead.

blogs.title: Angles Over Magnitudes: A Friendly Guide to Hyperspherical Energy
blogs.description: Why do angles between neurons matter so much for image semantics? This post demystifies hyperspherical energy with intuitive visuals and the phase-vs-magnitude analogy, showing how keeping pairwise angles stable preserves a model’s understanding of the world.

blogs.title: COFT: Guardrails for Stable, High-Quality Personalization
blogs.description: Meet Constrained Orthogonal Finetuning (COFT), an OFT variant that limits how far weights can move from the original model. See how a simple radius constraint prevents collapse, makes training less sensitive to learning rates and epochs, and stabilizes DreamBooth-style personalization.

blogs.title: Faster, Cheaper, Better: OFT vs. LoRA vs. ControlNet
blogs.description: A practical comparison of fine-tuning approaches for text-to-image models. We break down parameter efficiency, convergence speed, data needs, controllability, and final quality—plus why OFT’s block-diagonal rotations often beat LoRA’s low-rank updates and adapter-heavy methods in both speed and results.

blogs.title: From Edges and Segments to Photos: OFT for Controllable Generation
blogs.description: How OFT turns rough control signals—like Canny edges, segmentation maps, and face landmarks—into precise, photorealistic images. We highlight the new control consistency metric and show where OFT delivers more accurate, faithful control than state-of-the-art baselines.

blogs.title: Implementing OFT Today: A Practical Starter Kit
blogs.description: A hands-on guide to using OFT in your Stable Diffusion stack: where to apply it (attention layers), how to use the Cayley transform, choosing the number of blocks, identity initialization, training tips, and when to enable re-scaled OFT for extra flexibility.

blogs.title: Composable Control: Stacking Orthogonal Finetunes for Multi-Skill Models
blogs.description: Explore the tantalizing idea of multiplying orthogonal matrices to combine different finetunes—personalization, style, and controls—without retraining from scratch. We discuss what composability could enable and the open questions it raises.

blogs.title: Zero Overhead at Inference: Deploying Personalized Diffusion on a Budget
blogs.description: Why OFT is deployment-friendly: once trained, its rotations can be folded into the original weights, keeping runtime cost unchanged. We cover memory footprint, on-device benefits, and how OFT helps teams ship controllable, high-quality models without new latency taxes.
